correctness.rationale: Each nonalgebraic Henson one-type is a triangle-free neighborhood. Splitting choices by the third shore proves the exact rectangle polynomial; inclusion–exclusion of star rectangles leaves only bicliques with both sides at least two. Those exist iff F has a C4 and have leading coefficient equal to its number of C4s. Inverse uses coefficient z^2 and independence of powers (1+z)^d; exhaustively generated patterns on at most five defect vertices show the unique sharp first fibre. For the witness family the graph degree-cube moment differs by exactly 6 for every third-shore size. Actual standard-library verification passed for 220 direct finite graphs, 22 positive-C4 cases and all witnesses through c=7. Infinite claims rest on algebraic proof, not finite extrapolation.

evidence: Published 2026-10-04 general Henson polynomial covers the neighborhood/subset identification only; 2026-11-17 forest-defect result proves homotopy type and persistence of clique-free complexes, without determining their face polynomials. broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad Henson statement is computationally able to evaluate any finite instance, but does not logically specify this inverse classification or a first-collision theorem. Homotopy equivalence in the forest-defect paper is strictly weaker than equality of face-enumeration polynomials. The complete general biclique polynomial itself is prior/elementary and is not counted as original.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly specifies information retained by complete graded one-point types over a natural multipartite near-extremal K4-free parameter family, not merely a single computed count. It identifies a sharp four-cycle obstruction, recovers the complete missing-edge degree census, proves the unique first failure under fixed shores, and gives connected collisions at every larger size which differ in a degree-moment invariant. Such a reconstruction boundary and its infinite structural mechanism are useful independent of a downstream theorem.
